- 2.
 Security Officers should make themselves readily available to the crew, either by patrolling actively or by guarding departments. - 3.
 Security Officers are cleared to confine sentenced criminals in the brig for up to [bold]10 minutes[/bold].

 3.1
 For a sentence to be valid, it must be read aloud to the Warden or Head of Security. If done over radio, an audible confirmation must be received.

 3.2
 Security officers are responsible for ensuring that any sentences they themselves were involved in are properly documented in the Criminal Records System. - 4.
 When practical, Security Officers should patrol in pairs. - 5.
 Security Officers assigned to a department should prioritize the safety of that department, but are expected to assist other officers in times of crisis.

 5.1
 Security officers assigned to a department are forbidden from using their department access to acquire items or equipment otherwise restricted to that department.

 5.2
 Security officers assigned to a department are expected to comply with all reasonable requests of the department head, so long as they do not interfere with their primary duties as a Security Officer.

 5.3
 Security officers assigned to a department are to refuse any illegal raids, searches, or access of personnel or property within that department, and are expected to report any such requests to the Head of Security.
